methods.name: VLA policies
methods.description: Vision-Language-Action policies, a type of generalist robotic manipulation model.

methods.name: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT)
methods.description: A method used to make preferences learnable for robotic policies.

methods.name: Mixed training
methods.description: A training strategy that combines different types of data or objectives.

methods.name: Sequential adaptation
methods.description: A training strategy where models are adapted sequentially.

methods.name: Contextual prompts
methods.description: Prompts that provide additional context to guide policy behavior.

methods.name: Preference-only training
methods.description: A training strategy focused solely on learning preferences.

methods.name: LoRA
methods.description: Low-Rank Adaptation, a technique mentioned in relation to preference-only training.

methods.name: Procedural generation pipeline
methods.description: A pipeline used to automatically instantiate tasks and their preference-conditioned variants, generating demonstrations, metrics, and metadata.

methods.name: OMPL planner
methods.description: An Open Motion Planning Library planner used to generate trajectories within the data generation pipeline.

methods.name: Trajectory smoothing
methods.description: A technique applied to generated trajectories within the data generation pipeline.

methods.name: VLM grounding
methods.description: A process used to select preference targets within the data generation pipeline.

methods.name: VLM planner
methods.description: A Vision-Language Model planner used for preference-conditioned task planning within the data generation pipeline.

methods.name: VLM checker
methods.description: A Vision-Language Model checker used to verify skill satisfaction within the data generation pipeline.

datasets.name: LIBERO-PeRM
datasets.description: A benchmark for personalized robotic manipulation, comprising five task suites and 312 preference-conditioned tasks with pipeline-generated, human-reviewed demonstrations.

datasets.name: LIBERO-SinglePref
datasets.description: A task suite within LIBERO-PeRM for evaluating single-preference learning.

datasets.name: LIBERO-PrefScale
datasets.description: A task suite within LIBERO-PeRM for evaluating preference learning efficiency and generalization across data sizes, tasks, and layouts.

datasets.name: LIBERO-PrefConflict
datasets.description: A task suite within LIBERO-PeRM for evaluating preference-preference and task-preference conflicts.

datasets.name: LIBERO-PrefCompose
datasets.description: A task suite within LIBERO-PeRM for evaluating multi-preference composition.

datasets.name: LIBERO-ComprePref
datasets.description: A task suite within LIBERO-PeRM for evaluating realistic preference-conditioned reasoning based on contextual language.

metrics.name: Preference satisfaction
metrics.description: A metric to evaluate how well a policy adheres to user preferences.

metrics.name: Task success
metrics.description: A metric to evaluate if the nominal task goal is completed.

metrics.name: No-preference retention
metrics.description: A metric to evaluate how well a policy retains performance on tasks without preferences.

concepts.name: Personalized Robotic Manipulation (PeRM)
concepts.description: The field of study focusing on enabling robots to execute tasks in ways that align with individual user preferences, habits, and constraints.

concepts.name: Preference learning
concepts.description: The process by which embodied agents acquire user preferences from demonstrations or other signals.

concepts.name: Zero-shot personalization
concepts.description: The ability of policies to follow preferences without explicit preference data.

concepts.name: Preference generalization
concepts.description: The ability of learned preferences to apply across different layouts and tasks.

concepts.name: Preference composition
concepts.description: The ability of policies to combine multiple preferences.

concepts.name: Preference conflicts
concepts.description: Situations where multiple preferences or a preference and a task goal are in opposition.

concepts.name: Observable preferences
concepts.description: Preferences that can be expressed in language, instantiated without changing the original task goal, evaluated automatically, and reused across tasks.

concepts.name: Motion Preference
concepts.description: A type of observable preference that constrains the physical properties of the trajectory (Pmotion).

concepts.name: Skill Preference
concepts.description: A type of observable preference that alters the execution behavior of a specific skill (Pskill).

concepts.name: User Profile
concepts.description: A type of observable preference that uses a user profile or context to guide subtask-level semantic choices (Pprofile).

concepts.name: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models
concepts.description: Models that integrate vision, language, and action for robotic control.

findings.name: Current VLA policies struggle with zero-shot personalization.
findings.description: Observation that existing Vision-Language-Action policies perform poorly when asked to follow preferences without prior preference data.

findings.name: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) makes preferences learnable.
findings.description: Finding that applying Supervised Fine-Tuning enables policies to learn and incorporate user preferences.

findings.name: Mixed training achieves better no-preference retention than sequential adaptation.
findings.description: Result indicating that a mixed training approach helps policies maintain performance on tasks without preferences more effectively than sequential adaptation.

findings.name: Mixed training improves performance with contextual prompts compared with preference-only training.
findings.description: Finding that mixed training, when combined with contextual prompts, leads to better task success and preference satisfaction than training solely on preferences.

findings.name: Mixed training can weaken motion-preference learning.
findings.description: Observation that while mixed training has benefits, it may negatively impact the learning of motion-specific preferences.

findings.name: Preference generalization, decomposition, and conflict handling remain difficult.
findings.description: Conclusion that current methods still face significant challenges in applying learned preferences to new situations, breaking down complex preferences, and resolving conflicting preferences.

findings.name: Broader layout diversity and matched no-preference data also help.
findings.description: Finding that increasing the variety of layouts and providing corresponding no-preference data can improve policy performance.
